conflicts.note: Operation Epic Fury — Day 110 (June 17, Wednesday). FROM KINETIC WAR TO A FRAGILE DIPLOMATIC ENDGAME — the 14-point US-Iran peace MOU text was released (signing set for June 19 in Switzerland); the last US strike on Iran was June 11 and the dominant risk has shifted to Israel-Lebanon (Israeli strikes killed at least 14 on June 16 and 4 on June 17). DAILY-COST CONTEXT: standby burn ~$95M/day now, but Epic Fury's PEAK burn ~$1.88B/day in the first 6 days vastly exceeded the Iraq War (~$410M/day) and Afghanistan (~$300M/day) averages. The Pentagon's latest OFFICIAL direct-military figure is $29B (Hurst, May 12); the phased tracker is ~$34.44B. CONSUMER/TAXPAYER COST over ~108 days is far larger: ~$132B (Moody's Analytics via NPR, June 17) / $113.3B (iran-cost-ticker.com). OIL: Brent peaked ~$118/bbl at end-Q1 — the largest inflation-adjusted quarterly oil spike in EIA data back to 1988 — and has since fallen nearly 40% from its conflict peak (TradingEconomics, June 16), settling $78.96 on June 16 (first sub-$80 close since March). DAY 110 PLACEMENT: 67 days past Desert Storm (43 days), 32 days past Allied Force / Kosovo (78 days), and 9.2x longer than the June 2025 Iran-Israel Twelve-Day War. — Operation Epic Fury — Day 103 (June 10, Wednesday). THE MOST INTENSE MULTI-FRONT EXCHANGE SINCE THE WAR'S OPENING WEEKS — Trump's 'largely finished' framing fully collapsed within 72 hours: a direct Iran-Israel ballistic-missile exchange (June 8), a downed US Army Apache over Hormuz (June 9), resumed US strikes on Iran (June 9), and Iranian strikes on US bases in Bahrain, Kuwait AND Jordan (June 10). NEW ESCALATION MARKER: Iran's ballistic-missile reach to Azraq Air Base, Jordan (~1,000km from the Iranian coast) is the war's DEEPEST Iranian strike — extending the active retaliation map to a third base-host country and undercutting US missile-attrition claims; all intercepted, no casualties. MARKETS RE-COUPLED TO THE WAR: US May CPI topped 4% (4.2% y/y, highest since April 2023) on the energy shock, and the S&P 500 fell 1.62% to 7,266.99 (Dow -1.87% / -953, Nasdaq -1.98%, VIX ~22) — a war-driven repricing after weeks of complacency; WTI settled $90.03 (+2.07%), Brent $93.10 (+1.8%). BLOCKADE: 8 tankers disabled / 134 redirected (Marivex June 8 = 7th, Settebello June 9 = 8th; 3 Indian crew missing). US KIA 13 (unchanged; 2 Apache pilots rescued); daily burn ~$120M/day; Pentagon cumulative ~$29B (official, May 12; dashboard modeled ~$72.3B). DAY 103 PLACEMENT: 60 days past Desert Storm (43 days), 25 days past Allied Force / Kosovo (78 days), and 8.6x longer than the June 2025 Iran-Israel Twelve-Day War. — Operation Epic Fury — Day 100 (June 7, Sunday). THE WAR'S 100TH DAY: a blockade-plus-skirmish equilibrium centered on the Strait of Hormuz. The June 5-6 cycle — IRGC drone harassment, US coastal-radar strikes at Qeshm and Goruk, and intercepted Iranian ballistic-missile salvos at Kuwait and Bahrain (all intercepted, zero casualties) — is the new tempo; Trump (June 6) called the war 'largely finished ... one way or the other.' DAILY-COST CONTEXT: Epic Fury's peak burn rate was ~$1.88B/day in Days 1-6 (now eased to a ~$95M/day weekend floor). For scale, per Brown University's Watson Institute / Costs of War (via Al Jazeera, Apr 28, 2026): the 20-year Afghanistan war averaged 'more than $300m per day' (~$2.3T total) and the eight-year Iraq War averaged 'about $684m per day' (~$2T total) — so Epic Fury's peak daily burn ran several times the Iraq/Afghanistan averages, while its $29B official cumulative remains far smaller. OIL CONTEXT: April 2026's Brent monthly average of $117.29 was the highest since June 2008 ($132.32, the absolute nominal monthly peak) per the EIA Europe Brent Spot Price FOB series; Brent has since bled to $93.09 (June 5 close). DAY 100 PLACEMENT: 57 days past Desert Storm (43 days), 22 days past NATO Allied Force / Kosovo (78 days), and 8.3x longer than the June 2025 Iran-Israel Twelve-Day War. MARKETS (June 5): S&P 500 -2.64% to 7,383.74 (worst day since October — a chip/rates move, not a war shock), Brent $93.09, WTI $90.54, AAA gas $4.174. US KIA 13; Pentagon cumulative ~$29B (official, May 12). Two-carrier Arabian Sea posture (Lincoln + Bush) holds; no US carrier sits in the Persian Gulf. — Operation Epic Fury — Day 96 (June 3, Wednesday). CONTESTED CEASEFIRE, KINETIC EXCHANGES INTENSIFY — Iran's drone/missile strike on Kuwait International Airport killed one Indian national and wounded 63+; the US struck an Iranian oil tanker off Qeshm; and the US House passed an Iran war-powers resolution 215-208 (the first successful such vote). Oil climbed back toward $100 (Brent ~$97.98, +2.1%) and the S&P 500 snapped a nine-day record-setting win streak (-0.74%). MILESTONES: the war's 100th day arrives this week (June 7); at 96 days it is now 53 days past Desert Storm (43 days), 18 days past NATO Allied Force / Kosovo (78 days), and 8.0x longer than the June 2025 Iran-Israel Twelve-Day War. PRICE CONTEXT: the May 6 gas peak of $4.536/gal remains below AAA's all-time record of $5.016 (June 14, 2022), and crude — though back near $100 — is still well below the war's ~$126/bbl Brent peak (April). MARKETS (June 3): S&P 500 -0.74%, Dow -620.72 (-1.21%), Nasdaq -0.89%; defense (LMT +14.9% YTD) and oil majors outperformed. US KIA 13. DAILY BURN ~$150M/day on the renewed exchanges (CSIS ceasefire band); Pentagon cumulative ~$29B (official, May 12). Two-carrier Arabian Sea posture (Lincoln + Bush) holds; no US carrier sits in the Persian Gulf. — Operation Epic Fury — Day 95 (June 2, Tuesday). CEASEFIRE IN LIMBO, NOT COLLAPSE — the Pakistan-mediated 60-day extension MOU neither formalized nor fully collapsed in this window. June 1: Iran (via IRGC-linked Tasnim) suspended indirect talks and said it was 'opening other fronts'; Trump countered that talks continued 'at a rapid pace' and told ABC News (June 2) a deal to reopen Hormuz and extend the ceasefire was reachable 'over the next week' (a regional source told CNN talks were 'back on track'). Low-level kinetic exchanges continued — new US 'measured and deliberate' self-defense strikes at Goruk and on Qeshm Island (May 30-31) and an intercepted IRGC missile/drone attack on Kuwait (June 1). ANALYSIS: Samir Puri (King's College London) characterized the post-ceasefire strikes as 'tit-for-tat military-to-military engagements rather than attacks on infrastructure or widespread destruction en masse,' unfolding on 'parallel tracks' — military and negotiating — simultaneously. Consensus from CSIS, CFR, and the Soufan Center: the US achieved tactical damage but could not reach Iran's deeply buried (400-1,500 ft) underground missile infrastructure, eliminate the Strait threat, or produce its sought political outcome; CFR assessed the odds of achieving all/most campaign objectives as 'remote.' Goldman Sachs (Struyven/Grigsby, Apr 27 note via Bloomberg) projected Brent to average $90/bbl in Q4 2026 even if Hormuz reopens, and warned that if the ceasefire fails with ~2 million bpd losses Brent could average $115/bbl in Q4. DAY 95 PLACEMENT: 52 days past Desert Storm (43 days), 17 days past NATO Allied Force / Kosovo (78 days), and 7.9× longer than the June 2025 Iran-Israel Twelve-Day War. MARKETS (June 1 closes): S&P 500 record 7,599.96 (+0.26%), Nasdaq 27,086.81, Dow 51,078.88 — all records on a tech rally; Brent $94.98 (+4.24%), WTI $92.54 (+5.93%); AAA gas $4.322. US KIA 13. DAILY BURN ~$95M/day (Cancian/CSIS floor); Pentagon cumulative ~$29B plus ITEP consumer fuel burden ~$46.5B / $347.72 per household (May 31). Two-carrier Arabian Sea posture (Lincoln + Bush) holds per USNI June 1; Ford at Norfolk (maintenance), having concluded the longest US carrier deployment since Vietnam. — Day 94 (June 1, Monday). Iran suspended indirect talks/document exchange (Tasnim, 'opening other fronts'); Kuwait intercepted Iranian missile/drone fire (IRGC claimed a retaliatory strike on 'the air base from which the attack originated,' UNVERIFIED); oil surged on conflict fears while US equities hit record highs. — Operation Epic Fury — Day 91 (May 29, Friday). TENTATIVE 60-DAY CEASEFIRE-EXTENSION MOU REACHED BY NEGOTIATORS (UNSIGNED) — Trump in Situation Room for 'final determination'; announces US naval blockade 'will now be lifted' and stranded ships 'may start the process of heading home'; demands enriched 'nuclear dust' destroyed with IAEA, mines removed, no tolls in Hormuz, no money exchanged until further notice. Iran foreign ministry: 'we are focused on ending the war, and there are no negotiations on the nuclear issue' — no deal reached. Day 91 = 13 days past Allied Force / Kosovo (78 days), 48 days past Desert Storm (43 days), 7.58× longer than the June 2025 Iran-Israel Twelve-Day War. CARRIER POSTURE: USS Gerald R. Ford CSG (CVN-78) returned Naval Station Norfolk May 16 after 326-DAY DEPLOYMENT — LONGEST POST-VIETNAM U.S. carrier deployment, breaking USS Abraham Lincoln's 2020 record of 295 days (described by USNI/Military.com as the longest since the end of the Cold War; the all-time post-WWII record remains USS Midway, 332 days, Vietnam). CENTCOM retains 2 CSGs (Lincoln + Bush, 5th Fleet) — no replacement ordered. TOMAHAWK USAGE: WaPo reported 'more than 850 TLAMs in the first month,' later updated by WSJ to 'more than 1,000.' Per Stars and Stripes, the U.S. 'has fired more Tomahawk missiles during Operation Epic Fury than in any other military campaign in history,' ahead of Operation Iraqi Freedom (802) and Desert Storm (288) (CSIS, Cancian & Park). DAILY BURN: ~$100M/day ceasefire floor (Cancian/CSIS); cumulative ~$29B Pentagon official (Brown Costs of War: 'has totaled upwards of the Pentagon's estimates of $29 billion'); ~$72B independent through ~60 days (Semler/SPRI); Bilmes (Harvard): 'I am certain we will reach $1 trillion.' MARKETS: S&P 500 7,580.08 (+0.22%) — 4th straight record + 9th straight weekly gain (longest since 2023); Dow ~51,037 (+0.73%) — first close above 51,000 ever; Brent $91.82 (-0.95%) at 5-week low, -17% on the month (worst since 2020); WTI ~$87.36 (-1.73%). NO new kinetic naval engagements in or near Hormuz Days 79-80. conflicts.label: Iraq 2003 (43-day major combat phase)
conflicts.note: Operation Iraqi Freedom — major combat phase (Mar 19 – May 1, 2003, ~43 days). Targets ~19,948 munitions / ~41,000 sorties. US KIA 139 in major combat phase (full OIF 2003-2011 KIA: ~4,431). Cost figure reflects major-combat phase only (~$25B nominal, inflation-adjusted to 2026 $). Full-conflict cumulative (2003-2011) is materially larger at ~$815B nominal / >$1.3T 2026 dollars.

conflicts.label: Libya 2011 (222-day Unified Protector)
conflicts.note: Operation Odyssey Dawn → Unified Protector — NATO no-fly zone (Mar 19 – Oct 31, 2011 = 222 days). NATO total ~26,500 sorties; US strike contribution ~700–1,000 targets (limited US role after handover to NATO Mar 31). US KIA: 0. US cost: ~$1.1B nominal / ~$1.5B 2026 dollars over 222 days = ~$7M/day average.

conflicts.label: Gulf 1991 (43-day Desert Storm air campaign)
conflicts.note: Operation Desert Storm — 38-day air campaign (Jan 17 – Feb 23, 1991) + 100-hour ground war (Feb 24 – Feb 28). ~118,000 coalition sorties, ~38,000+ targets engaged. US KIA: 148 hostile + ~235 non-hostile = ~383 total US deaths during operation. Cost: $61.1B nominal (CRS RL33110); inflation-adjusted to ~$135B in 2026 dollars over 43 days = ~$3.1B/day. 700,000 coalition troops deployed.

conflicts.label: Kosovo 1999 (78-day Allied Force)
conflicts.note: Operation Allied Force — NATO air campaign over Yugoslavia (Mar 24 – Jun 10, 1999 = 78 days). ~38,000 sorties. US KIA: 2 (Apache helicopter crash, training accident in Albania). Cost: ~$3B nominal / ~$5.6B 2026 dollars over 78 days = ~$72M/day average. NATO no-fly zone enforcement + strikes on Yugoslav targets to halt Kosovo operations.

sources: Comparison conflicts use FULL-CONFLICT TOTALS (not Day-21 snapshots). Sources: CRS R44116 (Iraq), RL33110 (Gulf War), R41725 (Libya), RL30374 (Kosovo). Costs inflation-adjusted to 2026 dollars using BLS CPI-U. APPROXIMATIONS: Sortie-counts vs. distinct-target-counts are not always cleanly separable in DoD records; figures cited are best-available open-source estimates and should be read as orders of magnitude. Iraq 2003 cost row reflects ~43-day major combat phase only — full OIF 2003-2011 totals are materially higher (~$815B nominal). Libya 2011 'targets_struck' reflects US strike contribution only (NATO total sorties ~26,500). Iran 2026 row is current state at Day 100 (in progress) and will be updated daily until ceasefire is formalized.
